title: Midnight Umbrella Rollout — Preflight Checklist & Release Notes Draft
content:
Purpose:
This doc is the operational playbook and release-notes draft for the ‘Midnight Umbrella’ rollout: a coordinated, low-latency feature-wave that combines routing policy changes + two new model variants + a transient traffic grace period (umbrella) for customer sessions. Goal is zero user-facing regressions and predictable cost overhead during the 48-hour watch window.

Status note (quick):
- Draft: still awaiting infra sign-off and SRE load test results.
- Key blockers: model-variant footprint estimate from infra, final routing rules from platform, and legal review of customer comm language.

High-level rollout plan (timeline):
- T-7 days: Finalize release notes and comms; schedule release channel; complete dry-run on staging.
- T-3 days: Run full traffic-sim with 1.5x expected peak (12h).
- T-1 day: Freeze config; seed KV-cache warmers; preschedule canary traffic ramp.
- T: Launch at 02:00 UTC (low traffic). Enable umbrella grace window (10% extra capacity reserved for session handoff).
- T+1h: Evaluate canary metrics — increase to 10% traffic if stable.
- T+6h: If stable, move to 30% and disable umbrella reservations.
- T+24h: Full rollout if no regressions; otherwise hold and iterate.
- T+48h: Post-rollout review and remove temporary feature flags and umbrella quotas.

Preflight checklist (operational):
- Configuration:
  - [ ] Feature flags created + owners assigned (FF: umbrella.v1, routing-variant.b).
  - [ ] Routing policy manifests reviewed: ensure fallback chain includes model-compact and region-fallback.
  - [ ] Quota reservations for umbrella established in Dedicated pools.

- Infra & SRE:
  - [ ] Capacity simulation results attached (load-test id: INF-4123).
  - [ ] Autoscaler cooldowns tuned for ramp windows.
  - [ ] KV-cache warmer jobs scheduled and smoke-tested.
  - [ ] Pager duty rotations updated in case of regressions (see contact table below).

- Observability:
  - [ ] Dashboards prepared: per-model latency p50/p95/p99, cost-per-token, error-rate by route, tail-latency heatmap.
  - [ ] Canary alert thresholds defined: lat p95 +20% over baseline, error-rate >0.5% sustained for 5m, cost-per-token increase >15%.
  - [ ] Quickstart log search snippets (Elasticsearch / Splunk) included in runbook.

- Testing & Dry runs:
  - [ ] End-to-end smoke on staging with live-tooling (streaming responses).
  - [ ] Backfill test: ensure session affinity during umbrella handoff works across regions.
  - [ ] Failover test: force model-compact fallback and validate graceful degradation messages.

Customer-facing communications (drafts):
- In-product banner (short):
  "We're deploying improvements to our inference routing overnight. You may see transient differences in latency while we monitor performance. Reach out to support if you notice regressions."
- Email to customers on dedicated plans (long):
  - Subject: Planned rollout: performance improvements and temporary monitoring window
  - Body: short summary, expected impact (few minutes of latency variation), contact info, and a link to rollback SLA.
- Support play: templated response snippets for CS with known-issues list.

Rollout decision matrix (simplified):
- Green: All canary metrics within thresholds at T+6h -> proceed to 30% -> schedule full rollout at T+24h.
- Yellow: Minor cost/latency uptick (within 10–15%) but stable errors -> hold, trigger optimization (batching tweak) and re-evaluate.
- Red: Errors >0.5% or latency p95 > baseline +30% -> rollback flag; engage incident channel and call SRE.

Rollback plan (short):
- Action: Flip umbrella.v1 and routing-variant.b off, revert traffic to previous routing manifest, re-enable previous autoscaler curve.
- Post-rollback: run 30m validation, collect traces for triage, schedule hotpatch only if regression persists after reversion.

Telemetry sampling & cost guardrails (notes):
- Sampling: 100% sampling for canary cohort for first 6h, then 30% thereafter for post-rollout signal quality.
- Cost guard: temporary budget cap for Dedicated pools (explicit burn-alert at 12% over baseline). If breached, auto-throttle non-critical batch jobs.
- TODO: confirm chargeback labels are set so finance can attribute incremental spend.

Run-of-show for launch engineers (cheat-sheet):
- 01:30 UTC: preflight channel open, SRE confirms dashboards are green.
- 01:50 UTC: run KV-cache warmers (15m). Verify hit-rates >80%.
- 02:00 UTC: flip umbrella and enable 5% canary traffic.
- 02:10 UTC: smoke generation, check p50/p95, errors.

Contact table (primary responders):
- Oncall SRE: Priya Singh (pager)
- Release lead: Maya Owens (slack + cell)
- Serving runtime lead: Jordi Alvarez (github ping)
- Support escalation: Noah Kim (cs slack)

Release notes (draft):
- Short summary: This release changes routing to prefer lower-cost quantized variants for long-session requests and introduces an umbrella grace period to minimize session disruption during routing handoffs.

- What’s new:
  - Routing policy: session-aware routing allows stateful handoff across model variants.
  - New model variant (compact-b): 8-bit quantized variant with 20% lower cost and comparable p50 latency.
  - Umbrella grace window: temporary capacity reservation for session continuity during rollouts.

- Migration notes for customers:
  - No action required for most customers. Customers with pinned model versions should contact support to opt into the umbrella behavior.

- Known issues (pre-release):
  - Edge case: rare 502 from a transient cache miss during handoff (seen in staging at 0.02% of requests). Working on mitigation.
  - Cost: short-term uplift expected for Dedicated customers during the 48-hour watch window.

- Metrics to watch post-launch:
  - p95 latency by model version, error-rate by endpoint, cost-per-token over time, KV-cache hit-rate, session-resume success rate.

Notes to self / open questions:
- Confirm legal review for customer email copy (PRIVACY-23 flagged) — @Priya can you chase?
- Is the autoscaler curve change reversible without draining pods? If not, add explicit drain window.
- Explore adding temporary sampling headers to better trace session handoffs.

Appendix: quick links and snippets
- Canaries: Linear INF-4123 (traffic sim), GH PR#1892 (routing manifest), Confluence draft (technical appendix).
- Useful query: "errors AND model_variant:compact-b AND timestamp:[now-1h TO now]"

End of draft.

-- Maya O.
